rules.title: Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. amending Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63 – Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords, or for landlords to use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that uses nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential units. Each month and each unit counts as a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; competitor data is nonpublic data less than 90 days old
rules.penalty: City Attorney or aggrieved tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees and costs to the prevailing party.
rules.citation: Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.; Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63
rules.status_basis: Document shows the ordinance was passed to print and ordered published on November 18, 2025 (first reading); final adoption is not shown.

coverage.summary: Applies to coordinated pricing algorithms used for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable housing rent or income limit tools, and market research, appraisal or software development uses from the definition of algorithm.

rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
